**MEMORANDUM**

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 11, 2026
**Re:** Felound Regional Water Authority Services, Inc. / Zapeiv Chemical Corp.: issues in the PACl supply package (New York law)

---

## 1. Summary

I reviewed the Zapeiv package as a single deal:

- the Supply Agreement (SA);
- the Statement of Work (SOW);
- the Order Form (OF).

All three are dated March 1, 2026. The SA is governed by New York law (SA §16.1). The matter folder also contains Felound's Laboratory Instrument Maintenance Agreement with Ostrevka Analytical Instruments LLC. That is an unrelated vendor contract and does not bear on this deal, so I have not relied on it.

**The structural point that drives most of these issues is the order of precedence.** SA §17.2 says that if the Supply Documents conflict, the Supply Agreement prevails, then the SOW, then the Order Form. The SA is Zapeiv's general form. The OF and SOW hold the deal Felound actually negotiated: PACl only, Ostler Creek only, and a defined PACl specification. Under this ranking, the broad SA provisions override that narrower deal wherever the two conflict.

New York courts generally enforce an unambiguous contract according to its terms. Felound should therefore not expect a court to rescue it with the canon that specific terms control general ones, given an express precedence clause pointing the other way.

The four principal issues, most significant first:

1. **Exclusivity is far broader than the deal** (SA §4.1). It covers all water treatment chemicals at every Felound facility.
2. **"Specifications" means Zapeiv's own changeable data sheets** (SA §1.8). That definition displaces the SOW PACl specification for warranty and rejection purposes.
3. **Automatic five-year renewals with a 30-day opt-out window** (OF §2, read with SA §2.1). There is no termination for convenience.
4. **Zapeiv may assign freely** to any affiliate or business successor (SA §15.2). Felound may not assign without Zapeiv's consent.

Secondary points and client questions follow in Sections 3 and 4.

---

## 2. Principal Issues

### Issue 1: Exclusivity covers all chemicals at all facilities and overrides the Order Form's PACl/Ostler Creek scope

**Where it appears:**
- SA §4.1 (Exclusive Supply).
- SA §1.12 ("Water Treatment Chemicals").
- SA §1.3 ("Facility").
- SA §17.2 (Order of Precedence).
- Compare OF §4.1–4.3 (Exclusive Product and Covered Site).

**What it says:** SA §4.1 requires Felound to buy "one hundred percent (100%) of its requirements of **all Water Treatment Chemicals for use at any Facility** exclusively from Supplier." It also bars Felound from buying any such chemicals from third parties.

- "Water Treatment Chemicals" (SA §1.12) includes:
  - coagulants and flocculants (PACl, aluminum sulfate, ferric chloride);
  - disinfectants (sodium hypochlorite, chlorine);
  - pH adjusters (caustic soda, lime);
  - corrosion inhibitors (orthophosphate and polyphosphate blends).
- "Facility" (SA §1.3) means any plant, pumping station or related installation owned or operated by Felound **or any of its Affiliates**.

The Order Form sets a much narrower scope. The Exclusive Product is PACl coagulant (OF §4.1) and the Covered Site is the Ostler Creek Water Treatment Plant (OF §4.2). The SOW and pricing are also built around PACl at Ostler Creek only.

**Why it matters to Felound:**
- **The narrow scope does not control.** The two scopes conflict, and SA §17.2 ranks the SA first. Felound's exclusive purchase obligation would therefore be the SA §4.1 obligation, not the PACl/Ostler Creek obligation in the OF.
- **Felound would be in breach from day one.** It would breach if it kept buying chlorine, hypochlorite, caustic soda, lime, orthophosphate or alternative coagulants from its current vendors. It would also breach by buying any chemical for any of its other plants or pumping stations.
- **The breach could end the agreement.** A breach of this kind could support a Zapeiv termination claim under SA §12.1, or a damages claim.
- **Zapeiv has no matching obligation.** The OF has prices only for PACl, so Felound would be obliged to buy chemicals for which no price has been agreed. Zapeiv's supply commitment (SA §4.2) is tied to forecasts, and the SOW covers only PACl at Ostler Creek.
- **Existing contracts may be affected.** The clause could put Felound in conflict with its existing supply contracts for other chemicals and sites.
- **The obligation could extend beyond Felound.** Because "Facility" reaches Affiliates' plants, it could extend to entities that are not even party to the agreement.

**Recommended fix:** Narrow SA §4.1 to the Order Form scope, and make the OF control on scope. Proposed SA §4.1:

> "4.1 **Exclusive Supply.** During the Term, Customer shall purchase its requirements of the Exclusive Product for use at the Covered Site, each as specified in Section 4 of the Order Form, from Supplier, subject to Sections 4.3 and 14.2. Nothing in the Supply Documents obligates Customer or any of its Affiliates to purchase from Supplier any other product, or any product for use at any other Facility, and Customer and its Affiliates may purchase any other Water Treatment Chemicals, and any products for use at any other Facility, from any third party."

Make three conforming changes:
- revise SA §1.6 so that "Products" means the Exclusive Product;
- delete the Affiliate reach of "Facility" for exclusivity purposes;
- add the carve-out to SA §17.2 described under Section 3(a) below.

---

### Issue 2: "Specifications" means Zapeiv's own data sheets "as in effect from time to time," displacing the SOW PACl specification

**Where it appears:**
- SA §1.8 ("Specifications").
- SA §6.3 (Inspection and Rejection) and §7.1(a) (Product Warranty).
- SOW §1.2 (defined terms), §3.1 (PACl Product Requirements) and §8.2 (Acceptance Testing).
- SA §17.2.

**What it says:** SA §1.8 defines "Specifications" as "Supplier's **standard product data sheets** for that Product, **as in effect from time to time**."

SOW §3.1 sets out what Felound actually needs: NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 certified PACl, minimum 10.0% Al₂O₃, 70% basicity. However, SOW §3.1 does not use the defined term "Specifications." It describes "PACl Product Requirements" under a section heading. SOW §1.2 provides that capitalized terms take their SA meanings, and the SA's opening language to §1 applies its definitions across all Supply Documents.

As a result, every use of "Specifications" points to Zapeiv's data sheets, not to SOW §3.1. That includes:
- the conformity warranty (SA §7.1(a));
- the rejection right (SA §6.3);
- the SOW's own acceptance-testing clause (SOW §8.2).

If anyone argues that the SOW requirements conflict with the definition, SA §17.2 gives the SA definition priority.

**Why it matters to Felound:**
- **Zapeiv controls the quality standard.** It can lower the standard on its own by revising its data sheets, for example by reducing Al₂O₃ content or basicity. Felound would have no warranty claim and no rejection right for product that meets the revised data sheet but fails the SOW assay.
- **Remedies may not reach the certification.** The SOW contains a separate covenant to maintain NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 certification (SOW §3.2). However, the express warranty and rejection remedies run to "Specifications," so Felound's ability to reject and recover costs under SA §§6.3 and 7.2 for an assay or certification failure is doubtful.
- **Implied warranties are gone.** The disclaimer in SA §7.4 removes the implied warranties of merchantability and fitness for purpose, so Felound has no fallback.
- **This is a regulated process.** PACl dosing in drinking-water treatment is subject to the Safe Drinking Water Act and New York State Department of Health requirements. Off-spec coagulant can affect turbidity and treatment performance, and Felound needs a fixed, enforceable standard.

**Recommended fix:** Replace SA §1.8:

> "1.8 **'Specifications'** means, for each Product, the specifications and requirements set out in Section 3 of the Statement of Work (including, for the PACl Product, NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 certification, a minimum of 10.0% Al₂O₃ and 70% basicity), together with any additional requirements of Applicable Law. The Specifications may be amended only by a written instrument signed by both Parties. Supplier's product data sheets are for information only and do not modify or limit the Specifications."

Also make three conforming changes:
- amend SOW §3.1 to read "The Specifications for the PACl Product are: …";
- add to SA §7.1 a warranty that each Product, at delivery, is certified to NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 by an accredited certifier and is shipped from a certified manufacturing location;
- confirm that SOW §8.2 acceptance testing is measured against the revised definition.

---

### Issue 3: Automatic five-year renewals, a 30-day notice window, and no exit for convenience

**Where it appears:**
- OF §2.1–2.4 (Term).
- SA §2.1 and §1.4 (term delegated to the Order Form).
- SA §12 (Termination).

**What it says:**
- **Initial Term.** The Initial Term is five years from the March 1, 2026 Effective Date (OF §2.1).
- **Automatic renewal.** The agreement then "will renew automatically for successive five-year terms" and continues to renew indefinitely (OF §2.2).
- **Notice window.** Non-renewal notice is effective only if *received* "no earlier than 120 days, and no later than 90 days," before the then-current term expires (OF §2.3). That is a 30-day window. Notice is effective on receipt and must follow SA §17.3, meaning hand, courier, or email with a courier copy, addressed to the General Counsel.
- **Fixed-term termination only.** SA §12 allows termination only for uncured material breach (§12.1) or insolvency (§12.2). Felound also has a narrow right after more than 30 days of force majeure (§14.3). There is no termination for convenience.

The precedence clause does not help here. SA §2.1 and §1.4 expressly adopt the term mechanics "stated in the Order Form," so there is no conflict for SA §17.2 to resolve. The OF term provisions govern.

**Timing:** If the Initial Term ends February 28, 2031, the only opt-out window runs from about **October 31, 2030 to November 30, 2030**. A notice sent early is as ineffective as one sent late. If the window is missed, the agreement renews automatically for five more years, through about February 2036.

**Why it matters to Felound:**
- **A missed window is costly.** Missing the window, which is easy to do because the window opens and closes, locks Felound into five more years of exclusive purchasing.
- **The compounding risk.** If Issue 1 is not fixed, that renewal would carry the all-chemicals, all-facilities exclusivity.
- **Price exposure continues.** Pricing during renewal carries forward with annual PPI-based increases of up to 3% (OF §2.4, §3.3).
- **No other exit.** Felound has no way out short of proving a material breach.
- **The statute probably will not help.** New York General Obligations Law §5-903 limits enforcement of automatic renewal clauses in certain contracts for service, maintenance or repair of property unless the provider gives advance reminder notice. This package is mainly a contract for the sale of goods, so Felound should not count on §5-903.

**Recommended fix:** Replace OF §2.2–2.3:

> "2.2 **Renewal Terms.** At the end of the Initial Term, the Supply Agreement will renew for successive one-year terms (each, a 'Renewal Term') unless either Party gives written notice of non-renewal at least ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term. A non-renewal notice may be given at any time before that deadline.
>
> 2.3 **Termination for Convenience During Renewal.** During any Renewal Term, Customer may terminate the Supply Agreement for any reason on ninety (90) days' written notice to Supplier, without penalty, and Section 12.4 (Transition Assistance) of the Supply Agreement will apply."

The alternative is to drop automatic renewal entirely and provide for renewal only by mutual written agreement. As a further fallback, require Zapeiv to send a written reminder 30–60 days before the notice deadline. Also clarify the expiration date, for example: "the Initial Term ends at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on February 28, 2031."

---

### Issue 4: Zapeiv may assign freely; Felound may not

**Where it appears:** SA §15.2 (Assignment).

**What it says:** Felound may not assign without Zapeiv's prior written consent. Zapeiv "may assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, **without the consent of Customer**, to any Affiliate or to **any successor to all or part of its business**."

The clause contains no:
- exclusion for Felound's competitors;
- requirement that the assignee hold NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 certification, have manufacturing capacity, or be creditworthy;
- notice requirement;
- requirement that Zapeiv stay liable after assigning.

**Why it matters to Felound:**
- **Felound has no exit if the supplier changes.** Felound is bound to exclusive supply, with automatic renewal and no convenience exit. Zapeiv could transfer the contract, or part of it, to a thinly capitalized affiliate or to the buyer of a single product line. That transferee might be uncertified, lack capacity, or be a competitor, and Felound would remain bound to buy from it.
- **Partial assignment splits responsibility.** Assigning "in part" could leave delivery, tank management and warranty obligations with different entities.
- **Key protections may not follow.** The SA §11 insurance obligations and the SA §9 indemnity may not effectively follow an assignment to a weaker entity.
- **The clause is one-sided.** Felound cannot assign even in an internal reorganization without Zapeiv's consent.

**Recommended fix:** Make the clause mutual and conditioned. Replace SA §15.2:

> "15.2 **Assignment.** Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, by operation of law or otherwise, without the other Party's prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed; provided that Customer may assign this Agreement without consent to an Affiliate or to any governmental or public-benefit successor to its water treatment operations. Any permitted assignment by Supplier is further conditioned on: (a) at least sixty (60) days' prior written notice to Customer; (b) the assignee assuming all of Supplier's obligations in writing; (c) the assignee and each manufacturing location from which it will ship Products holding current NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 certification and satisfying the insurance requirements of Section 11; (d) the assignee not being a competitor of Customer; and (e) Supplier remaining jointly and severally liable for the assignee's performance. Supplier may not assign this Agreement in part. If Supplier undergoes a change of control or assigns this Agreement, Customer may terminate this Agreement on ninety (90) days' notice without liability. Any attempted assignment in violation of this Section 15.2 is void."

---

## 3. Secondary Points

**(a) Revise the order of precedence itself (SA §17.2).** Even with the fixes above, the ranking invites future conflicts. Add a carve-out:

> "…provided, however, that the Statement of Work controls as to Specifications and services, and the Order Form controls as to Term, Renewal Terms, pricing, the Exclusive Product and the Covered Site."

**(b) No termination for convenience generally (SA §12).** Apart from the renewal-term fix in Issue 3, consider whether Felound needs an exit during the Initial Term for any of the following:
- regulatory changes;
- a treatment process change, for example switching coagulants;
- plant decommissioning;
- repeated nonconforming deliveries.

A "chronic failure" termination right, such as three rejected deliveries in any 12-month period, would be a reasonable ask.

**(c) Price adjustment (OF §3.3).** The price-increase mechanism is reasonable: an annual PPI-based adjustment with a 3% cap on increases. Two points to confirm:
- that adjustments run in both directions, so that decreases pass through;
- that the adjustment formula applies only to PACl, which ties back to Issue 1.

**(d) Transition assistance (SA §12.4).** Ninety days of continued supply at then-current prices is helpful. Confirm that it covers the SOW services, including tank management and telemetry, and not only Products.

---

## 4. Questions for the Client

1. **Current vendors and other sites.** Which other chemicals (chlorine/hypochlorite, caustic, lime, orthophosphate, other coagulants) does Felound buy, from whom, and for which plants? Are any of those contracts exclusive or long-term? This tells us how much exposure SA §4.1 creates today.
2. **Affiliates.** Does Felound have Affiliates that operate plants or pumping stations? What is the relationship to the Authority itself? The answer determines how far "Facility" reaches.
3. **Intended term.** Is a five-year initial term commercially acceptable? Would Felound accept any automatic renewal, and if so for what length?
4. **Specification detail.** Is "70% basicity" a minimum, a target or a range? Does Felound need further parameters in the specification, such as specific gravity, pH, or limits on metals or other impurities?
5. **Assignment.** Are any Zapeiv affiliates or competitors of particular concern? Does Felound anticipate its own restructuring or a transfer of operations that would require an assignment right?
6. **Notice logistics.** Who at Felound will calendar the OF §2.3 window and control formal notices under SA §17.3? This matters if Zapeiv will not move on the window.
7. **Effective date.** Is March 1, 2026 the actual signing date? We are now past it, and the date affects the term calculation, telemetry installation (SOW §5.2) and the timing of the first price adjustment.

# MEMORANDUM

**To:** Supervising Partner
**From:** Associate
**Date:** November 11, 2026
**Re:** Felound / Zapeiv PACl Supply Package: Issues for Comment (New York law)

---

## Scope and Approach

I reviewed the three Zapeiv deal documents as a single package:

- **Supply Agreement (SA)**, dated March 1, 2026
- **Statement of Work (SOW)**, for PACl at the Ostler Creek Water Treatment Plant
- **Order Form (OF)**, setting term, pricing and exclusive scope

The matter folder also holds a Laboratory Instrument Maintenance Agreement with Ostrevka Analytical Instruments LLC. It is a separate, non-exclusive services contract with a different vendor. It has no bearing on the Zapeiv deal, so I have not relied on it. One point of comparison may still be useful in negotiation. Felound's other vendor paper gives it mutual, consent-based assignment (Ostrevka §12.1) and a termination-for-convenience right (Ostrevka §10.2). Zapeiv's draft gives Felound neither.

**One structural point frames most of the issues below.** SA §17.2 provides that if the Supply Documents conflict, they govern in this order:

1. the Supply Agreement;
2. then the Statement of Work;
3. then the Order Form.

**The Supply Agreement therefore prevails over the SOW and the Order Form.** The deal-specific terms in the OF and SOW are where the commercial bargain appears to have been struck. Where the SA's general language is broader or less favourable, the SA language will control. We cannot rely on the narrower downstream documents to protect Felound.

The issues are listed in order of significance.

---

## Issue 1: Exclusivity Covers All Chemicals at All Facilities, Not Just PACl at Ostler Creek

**Where:**
- **SA §4.1** (Exclusive Supply)
- SA §1.3 ("Facility")
- SA §1.12 ("Water Treatment Chemicals")
- SA §17.2 (Order of Precedence)
- For comparison, OF §4 (Exclusive Scope)

**What it says:** SA §4.1 requires Felound to buy "one hundred percent (100%) of its requirements of **all Water Treatment Chemicals** for use **at any Facility** exclusively from Supplier." It also bars Felound from buying any Water Treatment Chemicals for any Facility from a third party. The defined terms make this very broad:

- **"Water Treatment Chemicals" (§1.12)** expressly includes coagulants and flocculants (PACl, alum, ferric chloride), disinfectants (sodium hypochlorite, chlorine), pH adjusters (caustic soda, lime) and corrosion inhibitors (ortho- and polyphosphate blends).
- **"Facility" (§1.3)** means any water treatment plant, pumping station or related installation owned or operated by Felound *or any of its Affiliates*.

By contrast, the agreed commercial scope is narrow. OF §4.1 makes PACl coagulant the "Exclusive Product." OF §4.2 makes Ostler Creek the "Covered Site." The SOW, the pricing in OF §3 and the volume estimate in OF §3.5 are all built around PACl at Ostler Creek only.

**Why it matters to Felound:**

- **SA §4.1 controls.** The SA and the OF conflict on the scope of exclusivity, and SA §17.2 makes the SA prevail. The OF's PACl-only, Ostler Creek-only scope does not narrow SA §4.1.
- **Day-one breach risk.** From the Effective Date, Felound would arguably be in breach for each of the following:
  - buying chlorine, hypochlorite, caustic soda, phosphate inhibitors or any other treatment chemical from its existing vendors, at Ostler Creek or anywhere else;
  - buying PACl or any other chemical for any of its other plants or pumping stations, or for any Affiliate's facilities.
- **The breach would be material.** It could give Zapeiv a termination right under SA §12.1 and a damages claim.
- **Felound would have no pricing protection for the extra products.** Zapeiv has priced only PACl (OF §3.1). Felound would be compelled to buy every other chemical from Zapeiv with no agreed price for any of them.
- **The supply and termination protections are thin.** The only third-party purchase rights are the shortfall cover in SA §4.3 and the force majeure carve-out in SA §14.2. Neither lets Felound keep its existing vendor relationships.
- **The exposure lasts for the full term.** Combined with Issue 2, it could run for five years or longer.

**Recommended fix:** Narrow SA §4.1 so it tracks the Order Form. Proposed replacement:

> **4.1 Exclusive Supply.** During the Term, Customer shall purchase its requirements of the Exclusive Product for use at the Covered Site, each as specified in the Order Form, from Supplier, subject to Sections 4.3 and 14.2. Nothing in the Supply Documents restricts Customer or any of its Affiliates from purchasing (a) any product other than the Exclusive Product, or (b) any product, including the Exclusive Product, for use at any Facility other than the Covered Site, from any third party.

In addition:

- Add a sentence to SA §17.2: "Notwithstanding the foregoing, the Exclusive Product and Covered Site stated in the Order Form define and limit the scope of Customer's purchase obligations under Section 4.1."
- Consider narrowing "Products" (SA §1.6) so it means the Exclusive Product, or products added later by written amendment to the Order Form.
- Make sure "Facility" no longer sweeps in Affiliates for exclusivity purposes.

**Question for the client:**
- Which chemicals does Felound currently buy, and from whom, at Ostler Creek and its other plants?
- Do any existing contracts conflict with SA §4.1 as drafted?
- Does Felound want any other Zapeiv products (now or later) brought within scope on agreed pricing?

---

## Issue 2: Automatic Five-Year Renewals With a 30-Day Opt-Out Window and No Convenience Exit

**Where:**
- **OF §2** (Term), especially §§2.2 and 2.3
- SA §§1.4, 1.11 and 2.1 (Term)
- SA §12 (Termination)

**What it says:**

- **Term delegated to the OF.** SA §2.1 says the Agreement continues for the Initial Term and any Renewal Terms "stated in the Order Form." SA §1.4 adopts the OF definitions.
- **Initial Term.** Under OF §2.1, the Initial Term is five years from the March 1, 2026 Effective Date.
- **Automatic renewal.** Under OF §2.2, the Agreement "will **renew automatically for successive five-year terms**."
- **Narrow notice window.** Under OF §2.3, a non-renewal notice is effective only if *received* **no earlier than 120 days** and no later than 90 days before the then-current term expires. That is a 30-day window. Notice must follow SA §17.3, which requires hand delivery, overnight courier, or email with a courier confirmation copy.
- **No convenience exit.** SA §12 allows termination only for uncured material breach (§12.1) or insolvency (§12.2). SA §14.3 adds an exit only for force majeure lasting more than 30 days. There is no termination for convenience.

**Why it matters to Felound:**

- **The precedence clause does not help here.** The SA expressly hands term mechanics to the OF. The OF's renewal provisions therefore *are* the Agreement's term; they do not conflict with it. SA §17.2 offers no fallback.
- **The window is short.** On my reading, the Initial Term ends on or about **February 28, 2031**. The only effective non-renewal window then runs roughly from **October 31, 2030 to November 30, 2030**.
  - The exact dates depend on how "five years from" March 1, 2026 is counted (expiry on February 28 or March 1, 2031). The drafting should remove that ambiguity.
  - Notice received too early is as ineffective as notice received too late. An early, cautious notice would fail.
- **Missing the window is costly.** Felound would be bound for five more years, to approximately February 2036, with no way out short of proving a material breach. Combined with Issue 1 as drafted, that commitment could cover all treatment chemicals at all Facilities.
- **Pricing keeps escalating.** OF §2.4 carries the existing documents into each renewal, and OF §3.3 lets Zapeiv raise the price by up to 3% every year. The terms are never re-opened for negotiation.
- **Procurement policy.** For a regional public-water operator, a self-renewing ten-plus-year sole-source commitment may also raise internal procurement-policy concerns (see question below).

**Recommended fix (in order of preference):**

1. **No auto-renewal.** Renewal only by mutual written agreement:
   > **2.2 Renewal Terms.** The Parties may renew the Supply Agreement for one or more successive renewal terms of one (1) year each (each, a "Renewal Term") by mutual written agreement executed before the expiration of the then-current term.

2. **Fallback: short renewals and a simple notice deadline.** One-year renewal terms, with an outside notice date and no "earliest date" limit:
   > **2.3 Non-Renewal Notice.** Either Party may prevent the next renewal by giving the other Party written notice of non-renewal at any time before the date that is ninety (90) days before the expiration of the then-current term.

3. **In all cases: a convenience exit during renewals.** Add a termination-for-convenience right for Felound during any Renewal Term. Add a new SA §12.6:
   > **12.6 Termination for Convenience During Renewal Terms.** During any Renewal Term, Customer may terminate this Agreement for any reason on ninety (90) days' written notice to Supplier, without liability other than payment for conforming Products delivered before the effective date of termination. Section 12.4 applies to any such termination.

4. **In all cases: fix the dates.** State the expiry date of the Initial Term expressly (for example, "ending at 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time on February 28, 2031").

5. **Optionally: a reminder obligation.** Require Zapeiv to send written notice of the upcoming renewal 150–180 days before expiry.

**Questions for the client:**
- What contract length is Felound actually prepared to commit to?
- Do Felound's procurement rules, or any applicable public-procurement requirements, limit multi-year sole-source contracts or automatic renewals?
- Who internally will diarise the notice window if some window survives?

---

## Issue 3: Zapeiv May Assign Freely; Felound May Not

**Where:** **SA §15.2** (Assignment), read with SA §15.1.

**What it says:**

- **Felound needs consent.** Felound may not assign "by operation of law or otherwise" without Zapeiv's prior written consent. There is no reasonableness standard, and no carve-out for affiliates or reorganisations.
- **Zapeiv needs no consent.** Zapeiv "may assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, **without the consent of Customer**, to any Affiliate or to **any successor to all or part of its business**."

**Why it matters to Felound:**

- **Felound cannot vet who supplies it.** Felound is locked into an exclusive supply relationship for a regulated drinking-water treatment process, and it has no termination for convenience. Yet Zapeiv could hand the contract to an entity Felound has never vetted.
- **No assignee safeguards.** Nothing requires the assignee to:
  - hold current NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 certification (which SOW §3.2 requires Zapeiv to maintain);
  - be creditworthy;
  - have equivalent manufacturing capacity and logistics (SA §4.2);
  - carry the insurance required by SA §11;
  - be anything other than a direct competitor or adverse party of Felound.
- **Partial assignment could split the deal.** Because Zapeiv may assign "in part," it could separate the supply obligations from the delivery and tank-management services. It could also transfer a fragment of its business together with the contract.
- **Zapeiv is not kept on the hook.** Nothing provides that Zapeiv stays liable after an assignment. Felound could be left with a weaker counterparty for warranty, indemnity (SA §9) and other claims.
- **Felound's own flexibility is limited.** The one-sided restriction on Felound could block an ordinary internal restructuring or a transfer of the Ostler Creek plant to an Affiliate or successor operator. It could also block a regional consolidation, since "operation of law" catches mergers.

**Recommended fix:** Make SA §15.2 mutual and conditioned. Proposed replacement:

> **15.2 Assignment.** Neither Party may assign or transfer this Agreement, in whole or in part, by operation of law or otherwise, without the other Party's prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed. Either Party may, without consent but on prior written notice, assign this Agreement in its entirety to an Affiliate or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business or assets to which this Agreement relates, provided that: (a) the assignee assumes in writing all of the assignor's obligations under the Supply Documents; (b) in the case of an assignment by Supplier, the assignee (i) holds, and will maintain, NSF/ANSI/CAN 60 certification for the Exclusive Product and for each manufacturing location from which it will ship to the Covered Site, (ii) meets the insurance requirements of Section 11, and (iii) is not a Competitor of Customer; and (c) the assignor remains jointly and severally liable for the performance of the Supply Documents unless the other Party releases it in writing. Supplier may not assign this Agreement in part. Any attempted assignment in violation of this Section 15.2 is void.

In addition:

- Define "Competitor" if Felound has any concerns on that front.
- Give Felound a right to terminate on notice, with SA §12.4 transition assistance, if Zapeiv undergoes a change of control or assigns to an assignee that Felound reasonably objects to.

**Question for the client:**
- Does Felound anticipate any reorganisation, consolidation or transfer of plant operations during the term?
- Are there particular companies Felound would not accept as a chemical supplier?

---

## Issue 4: Secondary Points

These are lower priority but worth raising in the same turn of comments.

| # | Where | Point | Suggested fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4.1 | OF §3.3 | The price adjustment is index-based, but only upward moves are capped (3%).
